atomicity.reason: Three separately violable facets of one artefact: write one record per fault to non-volatile memory, carry three named fields, and stay readable over the diagnostic interface after a power cycle; each clause could stand as a requirement on its own.
atomicity.suggestion: Split into storage (one NVM record per fault), content (cell or sensor id, limit id, value) and retrieval (readable over the diagnostic interface after a power cycle), or keep one 'fault record' requirement deliberately.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: fault record, non-volatile memory, diagnostic interface and power cycle are standard terms and the three fields are named.

feasibility.reason: A fixed-layout non-volatile record per latched fault is routine (the architecture realises it as a 64-entry ring) and conflicts with no other stated need.

parent_fit.reason: Delivers the story's observable 'stored fault entry naming the cell or sensor and the limit it crossed', adding the measured value and persistence across a power cycle.

unambiguity.reason: 'One record per cell-protection fault' does not say how a fault is counted when several cells violate in the same cycle or further violations occur while latched (the record carries a single cell or sensor id), and for the persistence-qualified overcurrent limit 'the violating sample' whose value is stored is undefined.
unambiguity.suggestion: Define a fault as the first violation that latches the supervisor (or state one record per violating cell and limit) and say which sample's value is stored for the overcurrent limit.

verifiability.reason: Pass/fail is observable: force a fault, read the record over the diagnostic interface, compare the three fields with the injected cell, limit and value, power-cycle, and read it again.

summary: Parent-aligned, bench-testable fault record that bundles storage, content and retrieval and leaves the unit of 'one record per fault' open when several limits are violated.
